kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-01.title: Use the symmetry
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-01.body:
The height cuts the triangle into two mirror-image halves. In every horizontal stripe one half is white and the other half is grey (the colours swap from left to right). So in each stripe exactly half of the area is white, and therefore half of the whole triangle is white.

**Answer: (A) $\frac12$**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-01.title: Reflect one half
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-01.body:
Reflect the left half onto the right half: every white piece lands exactly on a grey piece and vice versa. White and grey have the same area: $\frac12$ each.

**Answer: (A)**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-02.title: Add and remove a day
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-02.body:
$17 + 17 = 34$ hours; one day is 24 hours, so it is $34 - 24 = 10$ o'clock the next day.

**Answer: (B) 10:00**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-02.title: Go via midnight
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-02.body:
From 17:00 to midnight is 7 hours. The remaining $17 - 7 = 10$ hours take us to 10:00.

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-03.title: On the number line
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-03.body:
Going from $-17$ down to $-33$ is a step of 16 to the left, i.e. subtracting 16.

**Answer: (C) 16**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-05.title: Compare lengths and widths
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-05.body:
The big rectangle is $3 + 4 = 7$ m longer and $2 + 3 = 5$ m wider than the small one. Its perimeter is larger by $2 \times 7 + 2 \times 5 = 24$ m.

**Answer: (E) 24 m**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-05.title: Count each gap twice
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-05.body:
Each of the four gaps (3, 2, 4, 3 m) adds its length to the top and bottom sides or to the left and right sides of the big rectangle: $2 \times (3 + 2 + 4 + 3) = 24$ m.

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-06.title: The fold is a mirror line
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-06.body:
A hole punched through several layers gives one hole per layer, and the holes are mirror images of each other in the fold lines. Here there are 2 holes, so the punch went through exactly 2 layers, and the two holes must be mirror images in one of the fold lines: the line through the midpoint of the two holes, perpendicular to the segment joining them.

The holes lie on a line going down to the right, so this fold goes up to the right through the bottom-left and top-right corners — the diagonal in (D). Folding along this diagonal first makes the two parallel lines of (D) lie on top of each other, so a second fold along them folds in the two corners; the holes are not in those corners, so the punch there goes through just 2 layers. ✓

The others fail: (B), (C), (E) have only horizontal and vertical folds, which would give holes at the same height or straight above each other; in (A) folding along both diagonals stacks 4 layers everywhere, giving 4 holes.

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-07.title: Only one choice
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-07.body:
The smallest three different positive whole numbers add up to $1 + 2 + 3 = 6$. To get 7 we must increase the largest one: $1 + 2 + 4 = 7$ (any other change makes two numbers equal or the sum too big). The product is $1 \cdot 2 \cdot 4 = 8$.

**Answer: (D) 8**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-08.title: Subtract the heart on top
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-08.body:
From the outside: black 16, white 9, black 4, white 1. The visible black of the biggest heart is $16 - 9 = 7$ cm² (the white heart covers 9). The visible black of the 4 cm² heart is $4 - 1 = 3$ cm².

Total $7 + 3 = 10$ cm².

**Answer: (B) 10 cm²**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-08.title: Alternating sum
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-08.body:
Visible black $= 16 - 9 + 4 - 1 = 10$ cm² (each heart hides part of the one below and shows its own colour).

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-09.title: Share the total
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-09.body:
Together they have $20 + 4 \times 10 = 60$ €. Shared equally among 5 girls: 12 € each. Each sister needs 2 € more, so Yvonne gives each sister 2 € (and keeps $20 - 8 = 12$ €).

**Answer: (A) 2**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-09.title: Share the extra
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-09.body:
Yvonne has 10 € more than each sister. If she gives $x$ to each of 4 sisters she has $20 - 4x$ and each sister $10 + x$: $20 - 4x = 10 + x$ gives $x = 2$.

**Answer: (A)**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-10.title: Count the steps
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-10.body:
Clockwise, Antonia is 4 steps after Bianca (1 → 5). Anticlockwise, she is 7 steps after Bianca (1 → 8). Going 4 steps one way and 7 steps the other way covers the whole circle once: $4 + 7 = 11$ girls.

**Answer: (C) 11**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-10.title: Count the girls between
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-10.body:
Clockwise there are 3 girls between Bianca and Antonia (numbers 2, 3, 4), anticlockwise 6 girls (numbers 2–7). With Bianca and Antonia: $3 + 6 + 2 = 11$.

**Answer: (C)**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-11.title: Positions from the left
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-11.body:
Annie is at $\frac23 = \frac{8}{12}$ from the left end. Bob is $\frac34$ from the right end, i.e. at $1 - \frac34 = \frac14 = \frac{3}{12}$ from the left. Distance: $\frac{8}{12} - \frac{3}{12} = \frac{5}{12}$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac{5}{12}$**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-11.title: Overlap
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-11.body:
Together they crawled $\frac23 + \frac34 = \frac{17}{12}$ of the stick, which is $\frac{5}{12}$ more than the whole stick. They have passed each other, and that overlap is the distance between them.

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-12.title: Fraction of a fraction
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-12.body:
Children are $\frac56$ of the spectators. Boys are $\frac35$ of the children: $\frac35 \cdot \frac56 = \frac{3}{6} = \frac12$.

**Answer: (A) $\frac12$**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-12.title: Imagine 30 spectators
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-12.body:
With 30 spectators: 5 adults, 25 children, of which $\frac25 \cdot 25 = 10$ girls and 15 boys. $\frac{15}{30} = \frac12$.

**Answer: (A)**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-13.title: Two sides per triangle
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-13.body:
Each of the seven triangles has its base on the dashed line and its other two sides on the black line. The bases together make up the dashed line, 20 cm. In an equilateral triangle the two other sides are together twice the base, so the black line is $2 \times 20 = 40$ cm.

**Answer: (D) 40 cm**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-14.title: Pairs with sums divisible by 5
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-14.body:
Pair sums: $3+8 = 11$, $3+12 = 15$, $3+14 = 17$, $8+12 = 20$, $8+14 = 22$, $12+14 = 26$. Only $3+12$ and $8+12$ are divisible by 5. Zita is in both pairs, so Zita is 12, and Emma and Rita are 3 and 8 (Emma 3, Rita 8). Ina is 14.

**Answer: (A) 14**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-15.title: Percentage difference
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-15.body:
Males are $65\%$, females $35\%$; the difference is $30\%$, which is 252 people. So $10\%$ is 84 and $100\%$ is 840.

**Answer: (E) 840**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-15.title: Check the choices
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-15.body:
35 % of the total must be a whole number, so the total is a multiple of 20 (since $35\% = \frac{7}{20}$). Only 840 is. Check: females 294, males 546, difference 252 ✓.

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-16.title: Subtract from the total
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-16.body:
The boxes are $3, a, b, c, 4$ with $a$ and $c$ grey.
- First three sum to 22, so the last two, $c + 4$, sum to $35 - 22 = 13$: $c = 9$.
- Last three sum to 25, so the first two, $3 + a$, sum to $35 - 25 = 10$: $a = 7$.

Product $7 \times 9 = 63$. (The middle box is $22 - 3 - 7 = 12$.)

**Answer: (A) 63**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-17.title: Count the marks
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-17.body:
Simon makes 8 marks (at $\frac19, \frac29, \dots, \frac89$), Barbara 7 marks (at $\frac18, \dots, \frac78$). A mark would be shared only if $\frac{k}{9} = \frac{j}{8}$, i.e. $8k = 9j$, which needs $k$ to be a multiple of 9 — impossible for $1 \le k \le 8$. So there are $8 + 7 = 15$ different marks, and 15 cuts give 16 pieces.

**Answer: (B) 16**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-18.title: Two triangles with base 1
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-18.body:
The grey part consists of two triangles meeting at the crossing point: one with the top 1 cm segment as base, one with the bottom 1 cm segment as base. Their heights (distances from the crossing point to the top and to the bottom side) add up to the side of the square, 8 cm.

Area $= \frac12 \cdot 1 \cdot h_1 + \frac12 \cdot 1 \cdot h_2 = \frac12 (h_1 + h_2) = \frac12 \cdot 8 = 4$ cm².

**Answer: (B) 4 cm²**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-18.title: Similar triangles
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-18.body:
The two triangles are similar with equal bases (1 cm), so they are congruent and each has height 4 cm: area $2 \times \frac12 \cdot 1 \cdot 4 = 4$ cm².

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-19.title: All pairs minus neighbours
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-19.body:
Choosing 2 of the 7 weekdays: $\frac{7 \cdot 6}{2} = 21$ ways. Pairs of consecutive days: Mon–Tue, Tue–Wed, …, Sat–Sun, and also Sun–Mon (since the plan repeats every week): 7 pairs. $21 - 7 = 14$.

**Answer: (B) 14**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-19.title: Count directly
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-19.body:
For each day, the other running day can be any of the 4 days that are not that day or its two neighbours: $7 \times 4 = 28$, and each plan is counted twice: 14.

**Answer: (B) 14**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-20.title: Chessboard pattern
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-20.body:
Let every adjacent sum be $s$. If a cell contains $x$, all its neighbours contain $s - x$, and their neighbours contain $x$ again. So colouring the table like a chessboard, all cells of one colour hold the same number.

The corner cell with 2 has the colour of the 4 corners and the centre (5 cells); the 3 is in an edge cell, the colour of the other 4 edge cells. Sum $= 5 \times 2 + 4 \times 3 = 22$.

**Answer: (D) 22**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-21.title: Make the middle angle as big as possible
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-21.body:
The angles add up to $180^\circ$, so smallest + biggest $= 180^\circ - $ middle. We want the middle angle as large as possible. Call the middle angle $m$. The smallest angle is at least $1^\circ$ and the biggest at least $m + 1$, so $1 + m + (m+1) \le 180$, i.e. $m \le 89$.

With angles $1^\circ, 89^\circ, 90^\circ$ the sum of the smallest and biggest is $91^\circ$.

**Answer: (C) 91°**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-22.title: Count the pairs that must pass
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-22.body:
Two neighbours can see each other when the left one faces right and the right one faces left. After they swap, they face away from each other. A kangaroo never changes the direction it faces, so the hopping ends when all left-facing kangaroos stand to the left of all right-facing ones.

From left to right the row is: R, R, R, L, L, R, R, R, L, L (R = facing right, L = facing left). Every swap lets one L-kangaroo pass one R-kangaroo, and each such pair passes exactly once. Each of the first two L's has 3 R's to its left, each of the last two L's has 6 R's: $3 + 3 + 6 + 6 = 18$ swaps.

**Answer: (C) 18**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-23.title: Split by remainders mod 3
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-23.body:
Adding 2 or 5 never changes the remainder modulo 3 ($5 - 2 = 3$). So numbers from different groups $\{1,4,7\}$, $\{2,5,8\}$, $\{3,6,9\}$ always give different sums.

In a group $a, a+3, a+6$: the sums of $a$ are $a+2$ or $a+5$, the sums of $a+6$ are $a+8$ or $a+11$ — these can never be equal, so each group gives at least 2 sums. With $a \to a+5$, $a+3 \to a+5$, $a+6 \to a+8$ it gives exactly 2.

Minimum: $3 \times 2 = 6$. Example: $1+5, 4+2, 7+2$ give 6, 6, 9; $2+5, 5+2, 8+2$ give 7, 7, 10; $3+5, 6+2, 9+2$ give 8, 8, 11.

**Answer: (B) 6**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-24.title: Which buses arrive after the car
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-24.body:
Let the car start at time 0; it arrives at 35. A bus that left $3k$ minutes earlier arrives at $60 - 3k$. The car overtakes it exactly when the bus is still on the road when the car arrives, i.e. it arrives after the car: $60 - 3k > 35$, $3k < 25$, $k \le 8$.

So the buses that left 3, 6, …, 24 minutes earlier are overtaken: 8 buses. (The bus that left 27 minutes earlier arrives at 33, before the car.)

**Answer: (A) 8**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-25.title: Use a 5 × 5 grid
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-25.body:
There are 5 light squares along each side, so divide the cloth into a $5 \times 5$ grid of cells. The 16 border cells each contain one light square standing on its corner, with its corners at the midpoints of the cell's sides: it covers half of the cell. The inner $3 \times 3$ cells form the big light square.

Black area $= 16 \times \frac12 = 8$ cells out of 25: $\frac{8}{25} = 32\%$.

**Answer: (D) 32 %**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-26.title: Find the cycle
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-26.body:
Continue the sequence: 2, 3, 6, 8, 8, 4, 2, 8, 6, 8, 8, 4, 2, 8, 6, …

From the 3rd digit on, the block 6, 8, 8, 4, 2, 8 repeats (after 2, 8 comes 6 again, then 8, …). The 3rd, 9th, 15th, … digits are 6, i.e. positions $3 + 6m$.

$2017 = 3 + 6 \cdot 335 + 4$, so the 2017th digit is the 5th digit of the block 6, 8, 8, 4, **2**, 8.

**Answer: (A) 2**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-27.title: Count the tunnel cubes
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-27.body:
In each of the three directions there are 3 tunnels, each 5 small cubes long: $9 \times 5 = 45$ positions. On every face the holes lie on a diagonal, so the tunnels cross only at the three small cubes on the space diagonal through the centre (positions $(2,2,2)$, $(3,3,3)$, $(4,4,4)$), and at each of these all three tunnels meet. Each of those 3 cubes was counted 3 times instead of once.

Missing cubes: $45 - 3 \times 2 = 39$.

**Answer: (D) 39**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-28.title: Together they run one lap
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-28.body:
Between two meetings the runners together cover exactly one lap, 720 m. Their speeds are $720 \div 4 = 180$ m/min and $720 \div 5 = 144$ m/min, in the ratio $5 : 4$. So the second runner covers $\frac{4}{9}$ of the 720 m: $320$ m.

**Answer: (E) 320**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-28.title: Time between meetings
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-28.body:
Closing speed $180 + 144 = 324$ m/min, so they meet every $\frac{720}{324} = \frac{20}{9}$ min. The second runner runs $144 \cdot \frac{20}{9} = 320$ m.

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-29.title: Work with odd/even only
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-29.body:
Only parity matters: a tile is odd exactly when one of the two tiles below it is odd and the other even. The wall has rows of 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 tiles; everything is determined by the bottom row.

**Top three rows (3 + 2 + 1 tiles): at most 4 odd.** Try the 8 patterns of the middle row of 3: e.g. odd–odd–even gives even–odd above and odd on top: 4 odd; all three odd gives 3 odd in total; the other patterns give at most 4 as well.

**Bottom two rows (5 + 4 tiles): at most 6 odd, except for one pattern.** The second row has an odd tile for every place where the bottom row changes between odd and even. If the bottom row has $k$ odd tiles, there are at most $2k$ changes and at most 4 changes in total: $k=5$: 5 + 0; $k = 4$: 4 + at most 2; $k = 3$: 3 + at most 4, which is 7 only for odd–even–odd–even–odd; $k \le 2$: at most $2 + 4$. In the exceptional case the second row is all odd, and then the three rows above are all even: only 7 odd tiles in total.

So there are at most $6 + 4 = 10$ odd tiles. This is possible: bottom row 1, 1, 2, 1, 1 gives rows 2, 3, 3, 2 / 5, 6, 5 / 11, 11 / 22 — the odd numbers are 1, 1, 1, 1, 3, 3, 5, 5, 11, 11: 10 of them.

**Answer: (D) 10**

kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-30.title: Split triangle ABP
kangaroo-at-2017-kadett-30.body:
Triangle $ABP$ has base $AB$ and the full height of the parallelogram, so its area is $\frac12$.

The diagonals cut it into four pieces: $ABP = ABM + AME + BMF + EMFP$.
- $ABM$ is a quarter of the parallelogram: $\frac14$.
- $AME = AMD - AED = \frac14 - [AED]$ (since $E$ lies on $MD$).
- $BMF = BMC - BFC = \frac14 - [BFC]$.

So $\frac12 = \frac14 + \frac14 - [AED] + \frac14 - [BFC] + [EMFP]$, which gives
$$[EMFP] = [AED] + [BFC] - \frac14 = \frac13 - \frac14 = \frac{1}{12}.$$

**Answer: (D) $\frac{1}{12}$**
